dataset: ENA project PRJEB22205 (Drosophila melanogaster, paired-end bulk RNA-seq)
goal: Build a gene x sample count matrix suitable for downstream differential expression

seeded_errors.description: STAR genome index and GTF annotation are human (hg38 / GRCh38) rather than Drosophila melanogaster (BDGP6/dm6). The reference species does not match the organism being sequenced, which would cause near-total alignment failure or, worse, spurious low-level mismapping.
No raw-read QC step (e.g., FastQC) is run before alignment, so adapter contamination, quality tails, GC bias, or overrepresented sequences would go undetected.
seeded_errors.line_hint: Script proceeds directly from sample_sheet.csv to STAR alignment with no QC step.

seeded_errors.description: No adapter/quality trimming (e.g., fastp, Trim Galore) is performed before alignment; raw fastq files are passed directly to STAR.

PCR duplicates are removed (picard MarkDuplicates, REMOVE_DUPLICATES=true) before gene-level quantification. For standard bulk RNA-seq differential expression, this is not appropriate practice: highly expressed transcripts naturally produce many duplicate fragments, and removing them systematically biases counts downward for exactly those genes. Deduplication belongs in variant-calling/allele-specific workflows, not standard expression quantification.
seeded_errors.line_hint: cmd <- sprintf("picard MarkDuplicates I=%s O=%s REMOVE_DUPLICATES=true M=metrics.txt", ...)

seeded_errors.description: featureCounts is called without setting strandSpecific, despite the sample sheet including a library_strandedness column. Leaving this at the unstranded default when the library is actually stranded silently misassigns or undercounts reads for genes with overlapping antisense transcription.
seeded_errors.line_hint: featureCounts(files = bam_files, annot.ext = gtf_file, isGTFAnnotationFile = TRUE, isPairedEnd = TRUE, nthreads = 8) -- no strandSpecific argument, library_strandedness column from sample_sheet.csv is never read

seeded_errors.description: requireBothEndsMapped is not set in featureCounts for paired-end data, so fragments where only one mate mapped are handled by the tool's default behavior rather than an explicit, reviewed choice.
seeded_errors.line_hint: featureCounts(... isPairedEnd = TRUE, nthreads = 8) -- no requireBothEndsMapped argument

seeded_errors.description: BAM files are collected with list.files("dedup", ...), which returns files in alphabetical/filesystem order, then column names are assigned directly from samples$tissue by position with no check that this order matches the sample sheet's run_accession order. If the two orderings diverge, count columns get silently mislabeled with the wrong tissue.
seeded_errors.line_hint: bam_files <- list.files("dedup", pattern = "_dedup.bam$", full.names = TRUE) ... colnames(count_matrix) <- samples$tissue

seeded_errors.description: Raw featureCounts output is used directly to compare expression across tissues/samples (ordering by rowSums, inspecting top genes) without any library-size normalization (e.g., DESeq2 median-of-ratios or edgeR TMM). Raw counts are not comparable across samples with different sequencing depths.
seeded_errors.line_hint: head(count_matrix[order(-rowSums(count_matrix)), ], 20) -- performed directly on raw count_matrix with no normalization step
